name: read_clip_tbl
title: Read the clipboard as a table

origin.description: Turn clipboard text into a data frame with read.table.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Character vector to parse. The default reads the clipboard.

Arguments passed to read.table. Defaults are header TRUE, sep tab, stringsAsFactors FALSE, na.strings c("NA", ""), strip.white TRUE, and quote empty. A leading tab on the first line sets row.names to 1.

origin.details: Column names are made into syntactic names. An empty clipboard returns NULL.
origin.value: A data frame, or NULL when the clipboard is empty.

translation.description: Turn clipboard text into a Frame using the same defaults as read.table.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: List of lines to parse. Omit it to read the clipboard. None means the clipboard was empty.

arguments.name: options
arguments.text: read.table options: header, sep, na.strings, strip.white, and row.names. allow_non_interactive is not accepted; set CLIPR_ALLOW to read the live clipboard.

translation.details: Defaults match clipr: a header row, tab separator, blank and NA as missing, stripped whitespace, and no quotes. A leading tab makes the first column the row names. Headers pass through make.names. Whole-number columns that fit in a 32-bit integer stay integers.
translation.value: A Frame, or None when the clipboard is empty.
translation.example:
from clipr import read_clip_tbl
x = ["Name's\tAge", "Alice\t30", "Bob\t25"]
print(read_clip_tbl(x))
